title: The sentence
note: What every English sentence needs, and the order it comes in

lessons.title: What makes a sentence
lessons.goal: Say complete sentences with a subject and a verb

lessons.title: Statements, questions, requests
lessons.goal: Change a statement into a question, a request or an exclamation

lessons.title: Word order: who does what
lessons.goal: Put the subject, verb and object in the English order

lessons.title: Phrases and clauses
lessons.goal: Join two short ideas into one longer sentence

title: Nouns and articles
note: a, an, the, plurals, and words you can’t count

lessons.title: Things you can and can’t count
lessons.goal: Stop saying “advices”, “informations” and “furnitures”

lessons.title: Plurals that break the rules
lessons.goal: Use the right plural, and know which words are always plural

lessons.title: My friend’s house
lessons.goal: Show who owns something with ’s

lessons.title: A or an
lessons.goal: Choose a/an by sound, not by spelling

lessons.title: When to say “the”
lessons.goal: Use “the” when both people know exactly which one

lessons.title: When not to use an article
lessons.goal: Drop the article with general ideas, meals and places like home

title: Pronouns
note: I or me, myself, this and that, who and which, some and any

lessons.title: I or me, he or him
lessons.goal: Use subject and object pronouns correctly, even in pairs

lessons.title: Myself, yourself: only when needed
lessons.goal: Stop saying “Myself Aditya” and use -self words correctly

lessons.title: This, that, these, those, one
lessons.goal: Point to things near and far, one or many

lessons.title: Who, which, that, whose
lessons.goal: Join sentences with who, which, that and whose

lessons.title: Some, any, much, many, few, little
lessons.goal: Talk about amounts naturally

lessons.title: Bored or boring? Adjectives
lessons.goal: Choose -ed or -ing adjectives, and put adjectives in the right place

lessons.title: Bigger, more careful, the best
lessons.goal: Compare two or more things without “more better”

lessons.title: Too, enough, very, so, such
lessons.goal: Say how much with too, enough, very, so and such

title: Present and past
note: The tenses you use in every conversation

lessons.title: Be, have, do: the helpers
lessons.goal: Use am/is/are, has/have and do/does correctly

lessons.title: Present simple: habits and facts
lessons.goal: Talk about routines, and never forget the -s

lessons.title: Present continuous, and when not to use it
lessons.goal: Use -ing for now, and stop saying “I am having a car”

lessons.title: Past simple: what happened
lessons.goal: Talk about finished events with the right past forms

lessons.title: Past continuous: what was happening
lessons.goal: Set the scene of a story, and interrupt it

title: Perfect tenses and the future
note: have done, have been doing, had done, will and going to

lessons.title: Present perfect: have done
lessons.goal: Talk about experiences and recent news with have/has + past participle

lessons.title: Since and for: how long
lessons.goal: Say how long with have been, since and for

lessons.title: Past perfect: had done
lessons.goal: Use “had done” only for the earlier of two past events

lessons.title: Will, going to, and plans
lessons.goal: Choose will, going to, or -ing for the future

lessons.title: When I reach, not when I will reach
lessons.goal: Use the present after when, as soon as, after, before and until

title: Questions and answers
note: Asking, saying no, question tags, and short replies

lessons.title: Asking questions
lessons.goal: Put the helping verb before the subject in every question

lessons.title: Can you tell me where it is?
lessons.goal: Ask polite indirect questions with normal word order

lessons.title: Saying no
lessons.goal: Make negatives without doubling or mixing forms

lessons.title: Question tags: isn’t it?
lessons.goal: Use the right tag instead of “isn’t it?” for everything

lessons.title: Short answers: So do I, Neither can I
lessons.goal: Reply naturally with “Yes, I do”, “So do I” and “Me neither”

title: Can, must, should, would
note: Ability, rules, advice, and sounding polite

lessons.title: Can, could, be able to
lessons.goal: Talk about ability and possibility, now and in the past

lessons.title: Must, have to, don’t have to
lessons.goal: Talk about rules and what isn’t necessary

lessons.title: Should, ought to, had better
lessons.goal: Give advice without sounding too strong

lessons.title: Would, could: sounding polite
lessons.goal: Ask for things politely and naturally

lessons.title: Should have, could have, must have
lessons.goal: Talk about past regrets and guesses

title: Verb patterns
note: to do or doing, make and let, used to, and the passive

lessons.title: Active and passive
lessons.goal: Say what was done when the doer doesn’t matter

lessons.title: To do or doing?
lessons.goal: Know which verbs take “to + verb” and which take “-ing”

lessons.title: Make, let, help, get
lessons.goal: Use make/let + person + verb without “to”

lessons.title: Used to and would
lessons.goal: Talk about old habits, and don’t confuse “used to” with “be used to”

title: Adverbs and prepositions
note: Where words go, and the small words in, on, at, to

lessons.title: Adverbs: how and how often
lessons.goal: Put adverbs like always, only and well in the right place

lessons.title: In, on, at for time
lessons.goal: Choose in, on or at for times, days and years

lessons.title: In, at, on, to, into: places
lessons.goal: Say where you are and where you go without “reach to”

lessons.title: Discuss, explain, depend on
lessons.goal: Use the right preposition after common verbs, or none at all

lessons.title: Joining ideas: and, but, although, unless
lessons.goal: Connect ideas with the right joining word, used once

title: If, wish, and reported speech
note: Real and imaginary situations, and telling what someone said

lessons.title: If it rains, we’ll stay in
lessons.goal: Talk about real possibilities with if

lessons.title: If I were you
lessons.goal: Talk about imaginary situations with if + past, would

lessons.title: If I had known, I wish
lessons.goal: Talk about past regrets with if + had, and use “I wish” correctly

lessons.title: He said that…
lessons.goal: Report what someone said, moving the tense back

lessons.title: She asked me where I lived
lessons.goal: Report questions and requests

title: Correct usage
note: Agreement, confusing words, and habits to unlearn

lessons.title: One of my friends is
lessons.goal: Match the verb with the real subject

lessons.title: Say or tell, make or do
lessons.goal: Choose between words that Indian speakers often mix up

lessons.title: Habits to unlearn
lessons.goal: Replace common Indian-English phrases with international ones

lessons.title: Small phrases, said right
lessons.goal: Use everyday phrases the way native speakers say them
